text:
deploy-bot: deploy started: release v2.17.4 -> canary slice=5% (prod-us-west) (job: deploy/2026-03-16-317)
incident-bot: ALERT: inference-runtime p95 latency > 1.8s across canary hosts for 3m. paging ryan (oncall)
ryan (oncall): I'm on it, joining. what scope?
alice.eng: seeing p99 tail increase and kernel_fallback_count spiking on canary nodes. noticed sustained microbatch queue growth.
ben.sre: confirming. dashboards show batching_window jumped from 8ms -> 120ms after the rollout on the canary cohort. kernel selector moved to fallback kernels on ~40% of requests.
alice.eng: paste logs: ```[2026-03-16T12:05:12Z] host-12 infer: batch_window=120ms queue_len=37 kernel=fallback:matmul_q8 -> latency=2200ms```
ryan (oncall): ok, hypothesis: new kernel selection heuristics in v2.17.4 are mis-triggering fallback under jittery microbatching. we should stop the ramp and cut canary back. options: flip feature-flag or kill-switch, or rollback.
ben.sre: product-lead, any customer pressure?
emily.cs: CS intake: three customers reported elevated latency for inference endpoints in the last 15m (low volume, high SLO sensitivity). no major errors, just slow. customers are waiting for update.
product-lead: priority is to reduce customer impact. flip kill-switch for canary ramp now.
alice.eng: to flip: `curl -XPOST https://ops.internal/flags/killflag.canary_ramp/disable -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN\"` or use /ops web UI.
ryan (oncall): running kill-switch CLI now. `opsctl flag set killflag.canary_ramp false --env prod --by ryan`
deploy-bot: killflag.canary_ramp set -> false. traffic slice for v2.17.4 reduced to 0% across prod-us-west. continuing requests routed to v2.17.3.
incident-bot: NOTE: automated rollback not triggered; manual rollback recommended if metrics do not recover in 5m.
ben.sre: within 2m post-cut traffic, p95 dropped back to baseline and kernel_fallback_count dropped to single-digit. microbatch window returning to ~9ms.
ryan (oncall): good. leaving canary at 0% and pinning v2.17.3. mark rollout paused.
alice.eng: root cause trace: selector change in kernel chooser (commit 9f7a2f) adds latency heuristic that mis-evaluates short spike in queue as long-running and forces quantized fallback kernels -> much heavier path.
product-lead: plan: revert commit 9f7a2f from release branch, run internal canary on staging, then gradual 1% ramp with enhanced tracing.
emily.cs: notifying affected customers with interim note (we cut canary and we'll update in 30m).
ryan (oncall): handoff: I'll stay on until metrics stable for 30m, then hand to ben.sre for longer-term postmortem. tagging eng-sre for follow-up.
ben.sre: created incident ticket INC-2026-317 with timeline and action items (revert commit, add guardrail in selector, canary test).
incident-bot: INCIDENT: INC-2026-317 created; severity P2; customers impacted: small subset (latency only).
ryan (oncall): summary: bad rollout -> kernel selector change caused fallback thrash under microbatch jitter. mitigation: kill-switch -> reduce canary to 0% -> metrics recovered. next: revert and harden selector heuristics + canary pacing throttles.
emily.cs: ETA for customer follow-up: 30m for initial update, 4h for RCA.
alice.eng: saving logs and sample traces to /var/incidents/INC-2026-317/ for postmortem.
ryan (oncall): closing thread for active paging; will update when handing to ben.sre. :white_check_mark:
